newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria harvests 2.65 mln T wheat, yield 3.18T/ha.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria harvests 2.65 mln T wheat, yield 3.18T/ha.

text.p: Bulgaria has harvested 2.652 million tonnes of wheat from two thirds of the area sown, giving a yield of 3.18 tonnes per hectare, the agriculture ministry said on Tuesday.
"We have collected 2.651,575 million tonnes of wheat from 833,440 hectares harvested so far," a ministry spokeswoman told reporters.
She said 67.9 percent of the sown area had been harvested, and 9,222 hectares of wheat had been affected so far by summer rainfalls and hailstorms.
In May, Agriculture Minister Ventsislav Varbanov estimated this year's wheat crop at around 2.4 million tonnes. Forecasts were based on an assumed average yield of two tonnes per hectare.

Wheat trade in the country is blocked as traders are concerned about expected poor wheat quality because of delayed harvest and summer rainfall and the fall in the mark against the dollar on the international markets, a Plovdiv Commodity Exchange (PCE) official said.

The minimum purchase price is set at 230 marks per tonne from this year's crop in a bid to secure the country's grain balance. Excessive wheat exports two years ago and a bad harvest in 1996 caused acute grain shortages earlier this year.

"Sellers refused to negotiate buyers' bids of 230,000 levs per tonne ex-works, hoping to sell at $135-$140 per tonne following the latest international rise of wheat prices, and the fall of the mark against the dollar," PCE chairman Krasimir Davchev told Reuters.
Under a fixed exchange rate system introduced on July 1 the Bulgarian lev was pegged at 1,000 to the mark.
Bulgaria's annual consumption is estimated at 1.6 million tonnes of bread wheat and 800,000 tonnes of feed wheat.
Bulgaria has to export some 232,000 tonnes of wheat this year under futures contracts agreed earlier this year. Poland has said it could accept cash payment for 100,000 of the total.
An export fee of 15 percent of international wheat prices has been set in a bid to curb exports.
